# Video to Image Sequence Online

> Free browser-based tool that extracts frames from video files as JPG or PNG
> image sequences. All processing runs locally via HTML5 canvas and Web Workers;
> video files are never uploaded to a server.

URL: https://www.videotoimagesequence.online/

## What it does

Converts MP4, MOV, and WEBM video into a numbered sequence of still images.
The user picks an extraction frame rate (FPS) and an output format (JPG or PNG),
and receives individual frames plus a single ZIP archive of all frames.

## Key facts

- Cost: free, no account, no signup, no watermark, no trial limit.
- Privacy: files never leave the device. Decoding happens in the browser, so no
  video data is transmitted over the network. Safe for confidential footage.
- Input formats: MP4, MOV, WEBM reliably. AVI/MKV only if the browser has the codec.
- Output formats: JPG (smaller, faster) and PNG (lossless, keeps transparency).
- File size: no server-side cap. The practical limit is the device's available
  memory, browser performance, video length, and codec support.
- Batch: multiple videos can be dropped at once and are processed sequentially.
- Install: none required. Works in any modern browser, desktop or mobile.
  Installable as a PWA.

## Answers to common questions

**How do I convert a video to an image sequence?**
Open the site, drop in the video, choose the FPS and output format (JPG or PNG),
click "Extract Frames Now", then download frames individually or as one ZIP.

**How many frames will I get?**
Video duration multiplied by the chosen FPS. A 10-second clip at 10 FPS yields
about 100 images.

**Should I choose JPG or PNG?**
JPG for general use, smaller files and faster downloads. PNG for VFX
compositing, game development, or machine-learning datasets, where lossless
pixel accuracy and transparency matter.

**Is it actually private?**
Yes. Extraction uses client-side JavaScript only. There is no upload step, so
nothing is stored on or sent to a server.

**Is there a file size limit?**
There is no server limit because there is no server upload. Very large or long
videos are constrained only by the device's own memory and CPU.

- https://www.videotoimagesequence.online/video-to-png — lossless PNG frame extraction

- https://www.videotoimagesequence.online/screenshot-from-video — capture a single frame
- https://www.videotoimagesequence.online/images-to-video — reverse: image sequence to WebM
